thread:
emma: Quick ping — I opened a docs PR for audit exports + consent flow and included Python/Go SDK snippets. Need legal + security wording signoff before we merge: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/842
pr-bot: PR opened by emma — https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/842 (labels: docs, compliance)
liam: skimmed the draft. main callout: avoid using 'PII' as a catch-all. For SOC2/controls please use 'customer-identifiable information' or 'confidential customer data'. Also, note that timestamp-only redaction can break ordering; we should call out sequencing risk.
sophia: legal note: we need a defined term in the doc (CII = customer-identifiable information) and a short sentence about required consent: "Exports of customer data require written customer consent or an explicit contractual clause." Can we add a suggested line?
emma: added a CII definition at top of the doc. Also added a `preserve_timestamps` param in the sample snippet — Owen, does the SDK/back-end support that field?
owen: SDK currently exposes `include_sensitive` and `mask_fields` for exports. Backend doesn't have a timestamp-only redaction path yet. For now we can show a client-side `mask_fields=['user_email','user_id']` example and note that server-side timestamp redaction is pending. I'll paste snippet I was thinking of.
owen: ```python
# python example
from redwood import AuditClient
import os
c = AuditClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'))
export = c.exports.create(
  scope='tenant',
  filters={'start': '2024-01-01', 'mask_fields': ['user_email','user_id']},
  consent={'granted_by': 'legal@acme.com', 'granted_at': '2024-11-01T12:00:00Z'}
)
print(export.id)
```

```go
// go example
client := redwood.NewClient(os.Getenv("REDWOOD_KEY"))
export, _ := client.Exports.Create(context.Background(), redwood.ExportsCreateParams{
    Scope: "tenant",
    Filters: map[string]interface{}{
        "start":"2024-01-01",
        "mask_fields": []string{"user_email","user_id"},
    },
    Consent: map[string]string{"granted_by":"legal@acme.com"},
})
fmt.Println(export.ID)
```

liam: thanks — two quick changes: rename `mask_fields` -> `redaction_fields` to match audit schema naming, and include an explicit note that redaction is best-effort and not instantaneous (raw data may persist until pipeline runs). Also recommend adding `consent.document_url` metadata to the export artifact.
emma: updated PR to rename to `redaction_fields` and added a paragraph about "best-effort redaction". Sophia — I added a placeholder for `consent.document_url`. Can you confirm acceptable wording for the consent requirement?
sophia: the wording looks fine. Please add the parenthetical: "(best-effort; raw records may be retained in encrypted storage until redaction pipeline completes)." Also require the export to include signed consent metadata: `consent.document_url` and `consent.granted_by`.
emma: added `consent.document_url` to the snippets and a short list of accepted consent forms (signed DPA, signed POA via legal@, or explicit support ticket with legal thread). I also added a small banner in the docs draft calling out that server-side timestamp redaction is pending.
mike: heads up from infra — backend needs a small schema change to accept `consent.document_url` and the `redaction_fields` array. I've opened INF-5982 for that work, ETA ~3 business days. If docs should not promise immediate availability we should gate the feature or mark PR as draft.
emma: set the PR to Draft and linked INF-5982 in the description. I wrote a short "Implementation status" callout in the doc. Recommend merge-as-preview once legal signs off.
sophia: ok to merge as preview with clear banner: "Preview: feature pending backend rollout (see INF-5982). Do not rely on server-side timestamp redaction until rollout complete." Keep statement factual; don't promise dates.
owen: I'll also add a short comment in the SDK snippet: `# server-side redaction: feature-flag pending` so examples don't imply full production behavior.
liam: :+1: make sure we also add a note that retention TTLs are policy-level and exports do not change retention enforcement.
emma: added sentence: "Exported data is governed by the tenant's retention policies; exports do not extend or shorten retention TTLs."
owen: final note — I'll submit a small follow-up PR to the SDK repo to add an example helper `mask_export_payload()` to make client-side masking explicit.
emma: awesome, thanks everyone. I'll squash and request an official review after adjusting the banner language and snippets. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/842 (draft, linked INF-5982)
pr-bot: emma updated PR #842 — now marked Draft (labels: draft, compliance)
liam: thanks — leaving review for final pass after the backend ticket is tracked.
